This message comes from Odoo, the all-in-one business management software platform.
Whether you're a small or large business, Odoo gives you one flexible platform built to grow with you.
Try today for free at odoo.com/nprpodcasts.
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
Police in Fairfield, California are investigating a shooting inside a Spirit Halloween store that killed one person and injured six.
Chief Dan Marshall says the investigation is just getting started.
We have no further information regarding the identity of the victims at this time.
Our thoughts and prayers are with the families of the victims of this heartbreaking incident.
There's also no known motive at this time.
Many states are still registering eligible voters for the midterm elections.
As NPR's Hansi Lo Wang reports, today is the last chance to register in North Carolina.
The window is closing today for eligible voters in North Carolina to sign up in person at the state's early voting sites.
They're set to close at 3 p.m. Eastern.
The only state where voter registration is not required is North Dakota.
And many states allow for same-day registration at the polls on Tuesday's election day.
If you're already registered, election officials recommend going to your state's official election website to confirm your status and contact information before casting your ballot.
Voters can be removed from lists, especially if they've recently moved, changed their name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
One of the nation's largest teachers' unions is suing the Department of Education for mismanagement of student loan forgiveness, and PR Sequoia Carrillo reports.
The suit was brought by Randy Weingarten, the president of the American Federation of Teachers.
It alleges that Education Secretary Linda McMahon has kept 90,000 public service workers from receiving student loan forgiveness.
Under Public Service Loan Forgiveness, or PSLF, qualifying public sector workers can have their loans forgiven after they make 120 monthly payments.
This case focuses on the PSLF buyback program that allows borrowers to retroactively pay missed payments and have those months count towards their total.
The suit alleges that rather than process those applications and forgive the loans, the department has paused efforts with little to no communication.
Sequoia Carrillo, NPR News.
France's Interior Minister is warning there's a very high risk of violence and public disorder around protest plan for today. NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
70,000 police are expected on French streets, including elite units as well as helicopters, drones, water cannon trucks, and armored vehicles.
The French nightly news is full of the kind of videos that worry the government, social media posts calling on young people to come out in costumes en masse to party, and some calling for chaos.
The confluence of Halloween with the protests has forced many cities to cancel Halloween celebrations and ban the sale of fireworks.
In Paris, where more than 100,000 demonstrators are expected in the streets, authorities are working to change the plan protest route to avoid the city center.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
You're listening to NPR.
The deciding Game 7 of the WNBA Finals tips off tonight between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream. Nina Thorson from member station KQED has this preview.
After her team lost Game 6 on Thursday, Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase said her players hadn't executed very well, but she was confident they would be ready for Game 7.
The physicality is supposed to be ramped up. These are win or die. This is do or die. This is it.
Whichever team wins, it'll be a milestone for their franchise.
The Atlanta Dream have been to the Finals three times, most recently in 2013, but they've never won.
The Golden State Valkyries have never been to the Finals, but this is only their second season in existence.
The Valkyries hope to get an edge from an enthusiastic home crowd that's already made them the most valuable franchise in the WNBA.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Thorson.
The game tips off at 8 p.m. Eastern, 5 p.m. Pacific tonight.
It has been a difficult week for Star Trek fans of both the original series and the sequels. First, Walter Koenig died. He played Ensign Pavel Chekhov in the original series during the 1960s. Koenig was 90 years old.
Three days later, Patrick Stewart, who played Captain Jean-Luc Picard, died. The Shakespearean actor became the face of Star Trek the next generation. He was 86. William Shatner, who played Captain James T. Kirk in the original series in the 1960s, called this a heartbreaking week.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
Everything falls through the cracks. Always say hello with Quo. Try it free at Quo.com/NPR.
